solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Only sort of aspiring to the latest style?

definitions.text: Only sort of aspiring to the latest style?

parts.words: Only sort of aspiring to the latest style?
parts.note: a phrase meaning 'only partly or loosely' is read literally as following a mode or trend

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly chasing the newest trend.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a rough, imperfect way, and literally means following a style, so it fits both the vague effort and the fashion picture.

clue.text: Pretend female will get time in power after deposing Queen

indicators.note: the queen is removed from the word for a time in power, as a monarch is deposed from the throne

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's period in power
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A political tale of a woman taking power once the queen has been overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time in power' reads as a phrase about tenure, but it is a single synonym; 'after deposing' then works on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to fake or simulate something, a close synonym of pretend as a verb.

clue.text: Circular line converted to square (but not initially)

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged
the bracketed phrase tells us to drop the opening letter of the word square

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle about turning a circle into a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not initially' cuts SQUARE to QUARE; 'converted' rearranges TO plus QUARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the great circle drawn round the Earth midway between the poles, an imaginary circular line.

clue.text: Pain yielding hearts — it's a high card

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, so the hearts letter is surrendered from the word

parts.note: an ache is a dull, continuing pain
H is the card-game abbreviation for the hearts suit

explanation.surface: A card player's discomfort at having to give up hearts, consoled by holding a top card.
explanation.definitionFit: In most card games the ace ranks as the top or a very high card in its suit.

clue.text: Dance a lot, jiving, according to the stories

indicators.note: jiving is dancing energetically, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Reports say there was a great deal of dancing and jiving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jiving' rearranges the letters of 'Dance' and 'lot'; 'a' stands alone at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on individual tales and accounts rather than on systematic data.

clue.text: Decomposing material smells badly around University

indicators.note: the word for stinking sits on either side of the university letter

parts.note: in British slang, to hum is to stink

explanation.surface: Rotting matter giving off a stench near a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hum' meaning to stink is everyday British slang, unfamiliar to many outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is the dark organic matter in soil formed by decaying leaves and plant remains.

clue.text: Dismissed start of Roman era in fury

parts.note: in cricket a batsman dismissed is out

indicators.note: start of signals that only the opening letter of Roman is used

parts.note: an age is a long period of history, an era

explanation.surface: The overthrow of the opening of the Roman period causes anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is intense anger or indignation, a strong synonym for fury.

clue.text: I'd knocked over stringed instrument, showing reduced concentration

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the letters of I'd are read backwards

parts.note: the lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A clumsy musician admits upsetting an instrument while not paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns ID into DI. 'Reduced concentration' sounds like a lapse of attention, but it is chemistry: a weakened solution.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, a dilute solution has been thinned with water, lowering its strength.

clue.text: Hostility in US Institute in Eastern US city

indicators.note: the institute's letters are placed inside those of the city

parts.note: NY is New York
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Bad feeling at an American institute in a city on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is the state of being an enemy, deep mutual hostility or ill will.

clue.text: One that's invested in munitions

indicators.note: invested here means enclosed or besieged, so the letters are concealed inside the word

explanation.surface: Someone who has put money into arms manufacture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' sounds financial, but it means wrapped inside: the letters are inside 'munitions'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing or the number one, as in the units column.

clue.text: Speed after crashing? Most of story provides support for figure

indicators.note: a crashing vehicle is wrecked, so the letters of speed are broken up and rearranged
most of says the last letter of the synonym for story is dropped

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A narrative about speeding and crashing, oddly supporting a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges SPEED to PEDES; 'Most of' trims TALE to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a statue or figure stands.

clue.text: What will pin down a Romeo among the reporters?

indicators.note: the womaniser sits next to the journalists in the answer, here after them

parts.note: the press is the collective term for journalists
a Romeo or womaniser can be called a stud

explanation.surface: A question about who will finally catch a philanderer working as a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin down' looks like capturing the Romeo, but it is a literal description of a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-stud, or popper, is a two-part fastener pressed together to hold fabric closed.

clue.text: Material presented includes opening of clever comic play

indicators.note: the word for what is offered contains the extra letter

parts.note: fare is what is offered or served up, as in television fare

indicators.note: opening of signals the first letter of clever

explanation.surface: A review of a script containing a clever start to a comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a comedy built on absurd situations and improbable plot twists.

clue.text: Praise insincerely, showing less depth

definitions.meaning: to compliment someone excessively to win favour
comparative of an adjective meaning level and shallow, more even

explanation.surface: A flatterer's compliments are shallow, lacking depth.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to compliment falsely, and the comparative adjective means more level or shallower.

clue.text: Hurried to consume last of sweet cake

indicators.note: the rushing word swallows the extra letter

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road

indicators.note: last of signals the final letter of sweet

explanation.surface: Someone rushing to eat the last of a dessert cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake, often made with ground nuts, in Central European baking.

clue.text: Start of recipe with garlic mayo encompassing very Italian dish

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of recipe
the mayonnaise word surrounds the letter for very

parts.note: aioli is a Provençal garlic mayonnaise

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction: begin with garlic mayonnaise around a very Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encompassing' puts V inside AIOLI to make AVIOLI; R goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels stuffed with meat, cheese or vegetables.

clue.text: Wild party? Cold awakening

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
arousal is waking up or stirring into activity

explanation.surface: After a wild party, waking up cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a drunken revel, a noisy and boisterous drinking party.

clue.text: Last character is nothing very big

parts.note: O, looking like zero, means nothing
mega is slang for huge or enormous

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that the final person is no big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person in a story but is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Wrong description of second-in-command?

definitions.meaning: a noun meaning a moral failing or sin
the prefix for a deputy, as in a deputy president or chairman

explanation.surface: Is it wrong to describe the deputy this way?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means wickedness or depravity, and as a prefix it marks a deputy, like a deputy captain.

clue.text: Contract snag?

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to come down with an illness

explanation.surface: A worry that a legal agreement contains a hidden problem.
explanation.definitionFit: One catches a cold as one contracts it, and a catch is a hidden snag in a deal.

clue.text: Component of avenue, say, is seen in stone road

indicators.note: the tree appears inside the abbreviation for stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight of 14 pounds
an avenue is a road lined with trees, so a tree is one of its parts

explanation.surface: A paving stone forming part of an avenue on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avenue' suggests a street, but here an avenue is a line of trees; one of them goes in ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town lined with buildings.

clue.text: Immediately aware of following publicity experts

indicators.note: following places the phrase for being aware after the publicity letters

parts.note: PR, public relations, are the publicity people
to be onto something is to have become aware of it

explanation.surface: Spin doctors are quickly wise to what is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for at once or without delay, from Spanish for quick.

clue.text: Wages: penny a year

explanation.surface: A grumble that the pay comes to a penny a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is the money earned for work, a general synonym for wages or salary.

clue.text: What might nevertheless be made up of thin sunshine?

definitions.text: What might nevertheless be made up of thin sunshine?

parts.words: What might nevertheless be made up of thin sunshine?
parts.note: the phrase for full daytime is read literally as wide sunshine, odd if the light is thin

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how weak sunlight could still count as full daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the full light of day, yet its first word is the opposite of thin, giving the paradox.
